correctness.rationale: In Poincare disk with q=tanh²(R/2), Stokes/geodesic-angle computation gives exactly A_n=Σ_j F_q(δ_j), F_q(δ)=2atan2(q sinδ,1-q cosδ), including a signed term when δ>π. Sorted angular gaps have Dirichlet(1,…,1) law, representable as 2π E_j/Σ E_i. With q=1−λ/n and typical E_j bounded by O(log n), F_q(2π E_j/Σ E_i) tends to 2atan(2π E_j/λ); exponential tail and Taylor remainder yield o_p(n^-1/2) on the empirical average. LLN gives Φ; delta method on Σ E_i yields influence g(E)−E[E gʹ(E)](E−1) and variance Var(g(E)−α E)>0. Area disk 4πq/(1−q) yields Ψ=λΦ/(4π). Monotonicity follows from decreasing arctan(y)/y and endpoint expansions of the exponential integral; λ→0 ideal-polygon and λ→∞ disk-filling regimes via bounded empirical spacings. Checked R≈log(4n/λ) and CLT tuning λ_n=λ+o(n^-1/2).

value.rationale: The coupling R~log n produces an explicit, strictly invertible disk-coverage phase profile and a fluctuation law in a natural random hyperbolic polygon model, distinguishing geometric finite-radius polygon behavior from ideal and disk regimes. The exact mean-only result is not the claimed addition.

final_claim: For a hyperbolic circle with n angularly uniform boundary samples, n sech²(R_n/2)→λ gives a monotone arctangent area-coverage profile, explicit endpoint regimes and a nondegenerate fixed-parameter Gaussian fluctuation.
limitations: Vertices are sampled independently uniformly in hyperbolic circle arclength at curvature −1; fixed critical-parameter CLT is not a universal fluctuation theorem for arbitrary hyperbolic convex sets.
